concepts.def: A body remains at rest or moves with constant velocity unless acted on by a resultant force.
F = ma. Resultant force on a body equals mass times acceleration. Vector equation.
Every action has an equal and opposite reaction. Forces come in pairs on different bodies.
Mass m is amount of matter (kg). Weight W = mg (newtons). On Earth, g ≈ 9.8 N/kg.
F ≤ μR (where R = normal reaction, μ = coefficient of friction). Limiting friction reached when motion impending.
Split forces into perpendicular components (e.g., horizontal/vertical or along/perpendicular to inclined plane).

walkthroughs.body_html:
Forces & Newton's Laws — a core area of A-Level Maths.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Forces & Newton's Laws brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Forces & Newton's Laws.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

mcqs.q: A 5 kg mass has resultant force 20 N. Its acceleration is:
options: 4 m/s²
100 m/s²
25 m/s²
15 m/s²

mcqs.q: On Earth, the weight of a 10 kg object (take g = 9.8) is:
What does the gradient of a straight-line graph tell you?
options: How steep the line is — the change in y for each unit change in x (rise over run).
Cats are the seventh most popular pet.
How long the line is on the page.
Where the line crosses the y-axis.

mcqs.q: How do you use a conversion graph between miles and kilometres?
options: Find the known value on its axis, draw a line to the graph, then read across (or down) to the other axis.
Look only at the gradient of the line and apply it as a formula.
How long the line is on the page.
Pick any point on the line — they're all equivalent.

sequence.def: Law 1 (1687): a body stays at rest or constant velocity unless forced.
Law 2: F=ma — net force gives acceleration.
Law 3: every action has an equal and opposite reaction.
Weight W=mg — a specific force acting on mass.
A resistive contact force opposing motion.
Splitting forces into components — the technique to apply all laws.
